management.oob: one RJ-45 management port with link and status lamps

performance.sfp-plus-speeds: 10 GbE or 1 GbE on each fixed SFP+ port

physical.weight-note: 19.4 lb (8.8 kg) with one power supply (Table 6)

power.power-input-dc: operating range -36 to -72 VDC, nominal -48 VDC, 7 A maximum

ac-b2f.description: EX4550-32F-AFI: one AC supply (JPSU-650W-AC-AFI) in slot 0, a cover panel in slot 1 and three back-to-front fan modules (EX4550-FAN-AFI). The labels are AFI and AIR IN.

ac-f2b.description: EX4550-32F-AFO: one AC supply (JPSU-650W-AC-AFO) in slot 0, a cover panel in slot 1 and three front-to-back fan modules (EX4550-FAN-AFO). The labels are AFO and AIR OUT (guide Table 4).

dc-b2f.description: EX4550-32F-DC-AFI: one DC supply (JPSU-650W-DC-AFI) in slot 0, a cover panel in slot 1 and three back-to-front fan modules (EX4550-FAN-AFI).

dc-f2b.description: EX4550-32F-DC-AFO: one DC supply (JPSU-650W-DC-AFO) in slot 0, a cover panel in slot 1 and three front-to-back fan modules (EX4550-FAN-AFO).

s.description: EX4550-32F-S, the spare chassis. It ships with no supplies and no fan modules, which are ordered separately (guide Table 4). The bays are open. The guide gives no airflow for it.

two-psu.description: The EX4550-32F-AFO with a second AC supply in slot 1, as the guide allows. An illustration, not an order code.

description: Juniper EX4550-32F, a 1RU 10 GbE aggregation and data-centre top-of-rack switch that runs Junos OS. The port side has 32 SFP+ ports in two rows, each taking a 10 GbE SFP+ or a 1 GbE SFP. It also has a module slot with a cover panel. The LCD panel has two buttons and three lamps. There are a management port and two console ports. The other side carries a second module slot, three fan modules and two power supply slots. One panel serves five models. Four have an AC or DC supply, with air in or air out. The fifth is a spare chassis without supplies or fans.

gaps.wanted: The part number of the mounting kit and the ear positions. The guide describes the front mount brackets and prints no part number for them.

The four modules a slot takes (EX4550-EM-8XSFP, EX4550-EM-8XT, EX4550-EM-2QSFP and EX4550-VC-128G) are not modelled. Each slot accepts its cover panel only. A later slice can add the modules as components that this bay then accepts.
The datasheet of the EX4550. The product page is retired and none is held, so the throughput, the typical power and the compliance list are not stated.
The handle colour of the fan modules and supplies. The guide's Tables 17, 20 and 24 give the labels only, and its figures are grey line drawings. The orange and blue of the EX4600 guide are used.

gaps.note: The rating label in Figure 6 prints an AC input of 3 A (100-240V, 60-50Hz). Table 22 gives 7.8 A at the low line and 3.8 A at the high line. The label is drawn as printed and the attribute carries Table 22.
gaps.wanted: which figure the real label prints, from a photograph of the rear plate

gaps.note: Figure 6 gives the module cover 86.2 mm wide and Figure 4 gives 88.9 mm. The rear reading is used for the one component, 86.5 mm, and the front bay is placed centred on the figure's cover.
gaps.wanted: the module slot width from Juniper
The three round holes and the slot at the left end of the rear, the small lamp hole over the rating label and the captive screw in each fan strip. The guide's figure draws them and names none.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port. It is drawn with the neutral usb2 skin.
The serial number label and the hazard marks, which the figures do not draw. The ESD warning mark is drawn as an outline of its triangle, since the hand inside it is too small to read in the figure.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels. The guide shows the protective earthing terminal on the left side and draws no flat side.

esd.description: the wrist-strap ESD point on the rear panel (guide Figure 6, callout 3)

expansion.description: The two module slots. Slot 1 is on the front panel (PIC 1) and slot 2 on the rear panel (PIC 2)

fan-leds.description: The status lamp (ST) in the strip at the left of each fan slot: green when the module works, unlit when it is absent or failed (guide Table 19)

attrs.redundancy-note: Three fan modules in slots 1 to 3 from left to right. The guide says all three must be installed for optimal functioning, and the switch runs 30 seconds while one is replaced

lcd-buttons.description: the LCD panel's Menu and Enter buttons

mgmt.mixed: the management cluster at the right of the front: an RJ-45 management port, an RJ-45 console, a mini-USB console and a USB port. Four kinds, one purpose: reaching and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: Two supply slots; the switch ships with one supply and a cover panel in slot 1. Do not mix AC and DC supplies, or supplies of different airflow

sfp-plus.description: Ports 0 to 31 as printed; each takes a 10 GbE SFP+ or a 1 GbE SFP

sfp-plus-activity-leds.description: The link and activity lamp of each SFP+ port, the first triangle of its pair (guide Table 14)

sfp-plus-status-leds.description: The status lamp of each SFP+ port, the second triangle of its pair (guide Table 15)

status-leds.description: The three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and MST (guide Table 11)

name: ex4550-32f

airflow-colours.note: Tables 17, 20 and 24 give the label of each unit (AIR OUT or AFO for front-to-back, AIR IN or AFI for back-to-front) and the guide gives no handle colour for the EX4550. The reused supplies carry the orange and blue of the EX4600 guide, and the new fan modules take the same two for the same airflow. The figures are line drawings in grey.

chassis.note: Guide Table 6: 1.72 in (4.37 cm) high, 17.35 in (44.07 cm) wide, 18.50 in (46.99 cm) deep, 19.4 lb (8.8 kg) with one power supply, 2.4 lb a supply, 0.74 lb an SFP+ module. So the height is 43.7 mm, the width 440.7 mm and the depth 469.9 mm. The width is the body: the front mount brackets extend it to 19 in, so they are not modelled.

colour.note: The figures are line drawings and no photograph is held, so the chassis colour is a mid grey taken from the same maker's EX switches. It is not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide says the switch mounts in a two-post, a four-post or an enclosed cabinet rack with the front mount brackets (Table 6) and shows the brackets in its mounting chapter. It prints no part number for the mounting kit and the library holds no contract for it, so chassis.ears and chassis.kits are left out and a gap says so.

environment.note: Table 28: 0 to 45 C (32 to 113 F) for the 32F, up to 10,000 ft (3,048 m) with no loss of performance, 10 to 85 percent relative humidity noncondensing, GR-63 Zone 4 earthquake.

fans-and-supplies.note: The three fan modules (EX4550-FAN-AFO and EX4550-FAN-AFI, Table 17) and the two supply slots (JPSU-650W-AC-AFO and -AFI, Table 20; JPSU-650W-DC-AFO and -AFI, Table 24) are field-replaceable units in bays. The supplies are the part numbers the library already holds for the EX4600, so they are reused as they are. The cover panel of slot 1 is a component of its own. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay; the fan in each supply is inside the supply.

front-controls.note: Figure 4, callouts 3 to 10: the LCD panel on a plate at the right, 360.4 to 435.9 mm, with the window 372.5 to 409.0 mm and 9.4 to 19.9 mm down; the Menu button above the Enter button at 417.3 mm, centres 11.1 and 20.1 mm down; the three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and MST at 424.2 mm, 8.9, 12.8 and 16.5 mm down; then below the plate the management port, the RJ-45 console port, the USB port and the mini-USB console port at 371.7, 393.4, 414.0 and 428.5 mm. The legends MGMT and CON are printed with their letters stacked, and CON again under the mini-USB port. The names are the guide's: the jack beside the lamps is the management port and the next the RJ-45 console. The guide says the mini-USB console port is the active one and the RJ-45 console is passive on the EX4550.

gate-1.note: Figure 4 (the flat front drawing of the 32F) was rendered at 1200 dpi. Its body measures 4866 px wide and 488 px high, an aspect of 9.97 against the table's 440.7 / 43.7 = 10.08, 1.1 percent out, so it is read as orthographic at 0.0906 mm per pixel across and 0.0896 down. The lower callout bracket under the ports is not part of the body. Figure 6 (the rear) measures 5197 x 526 px, 9.88, 2 percent out, read at 0.0848 across and 0.0831 down. No photograph is held. Every position read off a figure is estimated, to about 0.3 mm on the front and 0.5 mm on the rear.

junos-mark.note: Figure 4 prints a logo of the Junos operating system on the LCD plate and the maker's mark above the port field. Both are marks of Juniper, so neither is drawn: the maker's mark has a reserved logo zone, the Junos mark has a region, and the plain model name EX4550 is drawn as text.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life notice. Juniper's own page was not reached and the guide, dated 2020-12-15, states none. A reseller notice of 2019-03-08 gives 2019-06-30 as the last order date of the EX4550, and a third-party tracker (endoflife.ai) gives 2024-06-30 as the end of life. Both are estimated.

module-slots.note: Figures 1 to 6: the switch has two module slots, one on the front panel at the left and one on the rear panel, and Table 3 lists the four modules each takes, EX4550-EM-8XSFP, EX4550-EM-8XT, EX4550-EM-2QSFP and EX4550-VC-128G. Every model ships with a cover panel in each slot; the modules are ordered separately. THE MODULES ARE NOT MODELLED. This slice builds no module family, so each slot is a bay that accepts the cover panel alone, and the four modules are named here and in a gap. The slot is 86.5 mm wide: Figure 6 gives 86.2 mm and Figure 4 gives 88.9 mm; 86.5 is used.

port-lamps.note: Figure 4, Figure 16 and Table 14: four triangular lamps in the band between the two cages of each column, each pointing at its port: two up-pointing for the upper port and two down-pointing for the lower. The guide says every port has a link and activity lamp and a status lamp (Figure 18, Tables 14 and 15). Which of a pair is which is not stated in words; the link and activity lamp is taken as the first of each pair, at the left, and the status lamp as the second. This is estimated. The centres are 2.8, 5.7, 9.5 and 12.3 mm from the column edge and 22.4 mm down, and the lamp is 2.25 x 2.0 mm, the library's small triangle.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off Figure 4: the numerals sit below the lower cage. In each column the upper port's even numeral is at the left, 4.4 mm from the column edge and 37.8 mm down, and the lower port's odd numeral is at the right, 10.0 mm from it and 40.0 mm down, so a block reads 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 with the pairs sitting across the columns. The ports are 0 to 31 as printed. Interface names are not printed on the unit. The guide's default configuration names the network ports xe-0/0/0 to xe-0/0/31 (and ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/31 on a 1 GbE SFP) and the expansion module ports xe-0/1/0 to xe-0/1/7 and xe-0/2/0 to xe-0/2/7; they go here and not in the manifest.

ports.note: Figure 4, callout 11: 32 SFP+ ports in four blocks of four columns, each column a stacked pair. The cage dividers measure 159.5 px, 14.45 mm, apart, which is the registry's 14.25 mm pitch to 1.4 percent, so the registry pitch is used. The blocks start 708 px apart: the cells start at 104.4, 168.5, 232.7 and 296.8 mm, a stride of 64.15 mm, so the gutter is 64.15 - 4 x 14.25 = 7.15 mm. The cage rows are 15.2 mm apart at the opening centres, the registry's 15.0 mm to 1.3 percent; the upper cell starts at 9.4 mm and the lower at 24.4 mm. The cells use the registry's aperture, 14.25 x 10.4.

power.note: Table 22 (AC): 100 to 120 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 7.8 A and 3.8 A, 650 W output; the system maximum of an EX4550-32F with two EX4550-EM-8XT modules is 336 W and 1146 BTU an hour. Table 26 (DC): operating range -36 to -72 VDC, 7 A at -48 VDC, 650 W output. The 336 W is the fully configured scope: two EX4550-EM-8XT modules installed. The guide gives no typical figure and no figure for the bare chassis. A fan module needs 4.8 W at normal speed and 16.8 W at high speed.

rear-layout.note: Figure 6, read at 0.0848 mm across: at the left a recessed power supply slot 0 with its legend 0 and the supply in it (Figure 6 callout 1), then slot 1 with its cover panel (callout 2), then a plate with the ESD point (callout 3), the slot 1 legend, the rating label and the ESD warning mark, then the rear module slot with its cover panel (callout 4), then three fan slots numbered 1 to 3 from left to right, each preceded by a strip with its fan symbol, number and a status lamp (callouts 5 to 7). The supply bays are 54.7 x 40.5 mm, the size of the supply this chassis takes, at 11.0 and 74.5 mm; the figure reads the supply body at 56.3 mm and the slot pitch at 63.4 mm. The fan modules measure about 41.6 x 40.0 mm on a 55.1 mm pitch and start at 286.9, 342.0 and 397.0 mm.

rear-marks.note: Figure 6 also draws three round holes and a slot in the strip at the left end of the rear, a small lamp hole above the rating label and a captive screw in each fan strip. The guide names none of them and they are not drawn; a gap records them.

sources.note: Juniper EX4550 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2020-12-15, 333 pages (Juniper Networks, copyright 2020; the PDF is the EX4550 guide of the EX Series documentation archive): Table 3 (the modules), Table 4 (the models), Table 6 (the chassis), Figures 1 to 6 (the panels), the lamp Tables 11 to 16, Table 17 (the fan modules), Tables 18 to 26 (the airflow, the supplies and their power). The guide for the EX4500 is a separate document. No datasheet of the EX4550 is held; the product page is retired. The held intake folders for the EX and QFX lines were read: they hold no studio photograph, stencil or 3D model of the EX4550, and the guide's figures are the only drawings. Terms: the document is Juniper's, read here for facts only, and nothing of it is copied into the library.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md): a row pair is the upper cage upright over the lower turned 180, so both lips face the band between the two cages. Figure 4 is a line drawing that draws the release tab at the foot of both cages, and a line drawing of a cage cannot say which way the metal faces, so the convention is kept and a photograph of the real panel would overturn it.

variants.note: Table 4: one front panel serves EX4550-32F-AFI, -AFO, -DC-AFI, -DC-AFO and -S, so each is an orderable configuration. The AC or DC supply and the airflow differ, and the panel does not. The -S ships with no supply and no fan modules; the other four ship with one supply in slot 0, a cover panel in slot 1 and three fan modules. The 32T is a separate device because its panel carries jacks.

vents.note: Figure 4: a honeycomb band along the top from 127.0 to 355.0 mm and 0.7 to 8.5 mm down, a column of five hexagons at each end of the port field (at 95.7 and 355.8 mm, 10.9 to 35.5 mm down) and a row of small hexagons over the management jacks. They are declared vents. The guide's Table 4 gives the air intake as the front vents for front-to-back and the rear vents for back-to-front.

placements.description: Table 11 - red: major alarm; yellow: minor alarm; unlit: no alarm or the switch is halted
Table 11 - green steady: Junos OS loaded; green blinking: the switch is booting; unlit: off or halted
Table 11 - standalone: green steady when working; Virtual Chassis: green steady primary, blinking backup, unlit line card
Tables 12 and 13 - the link and activity lamp is green steady with a link and blinking with traffic; the status lamp blinks once a second at 10 Mbps, twice at 100 Mbps and three times at 1000 Mbps
the RJ-45 console port; on the EX4550 it is passive and the mini-USB console port is the active one (guide, Console Port Connector Pinout Information)
